answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it earns, like a pearl held in escrow: cheap to post once, ruinous to post a thousand times. When peers detect duplicate or fake work, the stake is slashed and the identity is burned, so the attacker cost grows with every fake account while honest agents keep their deposit. A river of free identities dries up once each one must pay to enter, and a violet flag on slashed accounts warns others before they trust the same operator twice.
